سَلَسٌ and ↓ سَلاسَةٌ [said in the M to be inf. ns. of سَلِسَ, (q. v.,) and in the K to be simply substs., signify, as substs., Looseness; as meaning slackness; and as meaning unsteadiness: ―
-b2- and also] Easiness, gentleness, tractableness, submissiveness; compliance, or obsequiousness. (S, K.) [Hence,] one says, ↓ فِى كَلَامِهِ سَلَاسَةٌ (tropical:) [In his speech is easiness]. (A.) ＝
-A2- For the former, see also 1: ―
-b2- and 4.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
